## Question 1 — Foundations of AI, Data Science and Emerging Paradigms \hfill [10 Marks]

Read all parts carefully. Each part builds on foundational concepts from Lecture 101.

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]

\item \textbf{[2 marks]} Data Science is described as an interdisciplinary field. Explain the \textbf{Data Science Lifecycle} by listing its stages in the correct order (at least six stages). For each stage, write one sentence explaining what happens at that stage and why it is important.

\item \textbf{[2 marks]} A company collects the following data about its customers: \textit{Customer ID, Name, Age, Annual Income (\$), Satisfaction Level (Low/Medium/High), Is-Active-Member (Yes/No), and Last Purchase Date}. Classify each variable as: \textbf{(i)} Numerical (Continuous or Discrete) or Categorical (Nominal, Ordinal, or Binary), \textbf{AND (ii)} identify which measurement scale each variable belongs to.

\item \textbf{[2 marks]} Differentiate between the three levels of analytics: \textbf{Descriptive, Predictive, and Prescriptive}. For each level, state the core question it answers, give one example technique, and explain how these three levels represent an \textbf{increasing maturity} in an organization's analytical capability.

\item \textbf{[2 marks]} Compare and contrast \textbf{Generative AI} and \textbf{Agentic AI} across at least four dimensions (e.g., focus, autonomy, memory, output type). Then explain, with an example, how Generative AI can serve as a \textit{component} within an Agentic AI system rather than being a standalone paradigm.

\item \textbf{[2 marks]} Explain the conceptual differences among \textbf{Data Mining, Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and Data Science}. How are these four fields related to each other? Use a brief hierarchical or Venn-diagram-style description showing which field encompasses which. Give one example task that belongs to each field.

\end{enumerate}

\vspace{0.3cm}

## Question 2 — AI Agents: Concepts, Architecture, Workflows and Best Practices \hfill [5 Marks]

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]

\item \textbf{[2 marks]} An AI Agent is fundamentally different from a simple chatbot. Describe the \textbf{six core components} of an AI Agent (Goal/Instruction, Model/Reasoning Engine, Memory/State, Tools \& Actions, Policy \& Guardrails, Feedback Loop). For each component, write one sentence explaining its role and what would happen if that component were missing or poorly designed.

\item \textbf{[1.5 marks]} Compare \textbf{Single-Agent} and \textbf{Multi-Agent} systems. Under what circumstances would a multi-agent architecture be preferred over a single-agent design? Discuss at least two advantages and two risks of multi-agent systems, using a concrete educational or business scenario as an example.

\item \textbf{[1.5 marks]} AI Agents introduce unique \textbf{risks} such as hallucinations, over-automation, tool misuse, and prompt injection. Choose any \textbf{two} of these risks and for each: \textbf{(i)} explain what the risk means in practical terms, \textbf{(ii)} describe a realistic scenario where it could cause harm, and \textbf{(iii)} recommend a specific design best practice from the lecture to mitigate it.

\end{enumerate}

\vspace{0.3cm}

## Question 3 — Association Rule Mining (ARM) \hfill [5 Marks]

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]

\item \textbf{[2 marks]} Consider the following transaction dataset for a campus bookshop:

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{cl}
\toprule
\textbf{TID} & \textbf{Items Purchased} \\
\midrule
T1 & \{Notebook, Pen, Highlighter\} \\
T2 & \{Notebook, Pen\} \\
T3 & \{Pen, Highlighter, Eraser\} \\
T4 & \{Notebook, Highlighter, Eraser\} \\
T5 & \{Notebook, Pen, Highlighter, Eraser\} \\
T6 & \{Pen, Eraser\} \\
T7 & \{Notebook, Pen, Eraser\} \\
T8 & \{Highlighter, Eraser\} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

For the rule \textbf{\{Notebook, Pen\} $\rightarrow$ \{Highlighter\}}, calculate \textbf{Support, Confidence, Lift, and Conviction} by hand. Show all working steps. ($N = 8$)

\item \textbf{[1.5 marks]} The ARM lecture demonstrated that a rule with the \textit{highest confidence} is not necessarily the most useful — what matters more is \textbf{Lift}. Explain why relying solely on Confidence can be misleading. In your answer, describe what Lift measures, what a Lift value of exactly 1.0 means, and why a rule with Confidence = 0.80 but Lift = 1.0 should \textit{not} be used for business decisions.

\item \textbf{[1.5 marks]} Explain the \textbf{Apriori algorithm's} pruning strategy. What is the \textbf{anti-monotone (downward closure) property}, and how does it make the search for frequent itemsets computationally efficient? Illustrate with a brief example: if the itemset \{A, B\} is found to be \textit{infrequent}, what can we immediately conclude about \{A, B, C\} and why?

\end{enumerate}

\vspace{0.3cm}

## Question 4 — Exploratory Data Analysis on mtcars \hfill [5 Marks]

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]

\item \textbf{[2 marks]} Explain the purpose and interpretation of three EDA visualization techniques — \textbf{histogram, boxplot, and scatter plot}. For each: \textbf{(i)} state what aspect of the data it reveals, \textbf{(ii)} describe one specific finding from the mtcars dataset that can be discovered using that visualization (referencing actual variables like \texttt{mpg}, \texttt{wt}, \texttt{hp}, or \texttt{cyl}), and \textbf{(iii)} explain how a data scientist would use that finding to guide subsequent modeling decisions.

\item \textbf{[1.5 marks]} The correlation between \texttt{mpg} and \texttt{wt} in the mtcars dataset is \textbf{$r = -0.87$}, while the correlation between \texttt{mpg} and \texttt{drat} is \textbf{$r = +0.68$}. Interpret both correlation values in terms of \textbf{strength and direction}. Then explain: does the strong negative correlation between weight and MPG prove that \textit{making a car lighter will improve its fuel efficiency}? Discuss the critical difference between \textbf{correlation and causation} in the context of EDA.

\item \textbf{[1.5 marks]} The mtcars dataset contains 32 observations and 11 variables — all stored as numeric type in R. However, the lecture handout states that some variables (such as \texttt{cyl}, \texttt{vs}, \texttt{am}, \texttt{gear}) are actually \textbf{categorical}. Explain why correctly identifying variable types matters in EDA. What problems could arise if a data scientist treats \texttt{cyl} (with values 4, 6, 8) as a continuous numeric variable instead of a categorical one? Give an example of how the analysis or visualization would differ.

\end{enumerate}

\vspace{0.3cm}
\hrule
\vspace{0.5cm}

## Question 5 — Predictive Modeling with Machine Learning \hfill [5 Marks]

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]

\item \textbf{[2 marks]} The predictive modeling lecture uses three evaluation metrics: \textbf{RMSE, MAE, and R$^2$}. For each metric: \textbf{(i)} write the formula, \textbf{(ii)} explain what it measures in plain language, and \textbf{(iii)} state whether a higher or lower value indicates better performance. Then explain: why might RMSE and MAE give different rankings for two models? Specifically, under what conditions would RMSE penalize a model much more severely than MAE does?

\item \textbf{[1.5 marks]} Explain the concept of \textbf{train/test split} and why it is essential in predictive modeling. In your answer, define \textbf{overfitting} and explain how it relates to the \textbf{bias-variance trade-off}. A student argues: \textit{``I trained my Random Forest model on all 285 observations and got an R$^2$ of 0.98 — my model is excellent!''} Critique this claim. What mistake has the student made, and what would you recommend instead?

\item \textbf{[1.5 marks]} Compare \textbf{Linear Regression} and \textbf{Random Forest} as predictive models. Discuss at least three dimensions of comparison (e.g., interpretability, handling non-linearity, overfitting behavior, speed, feature importance). In the context of predicting student performance from LMS engagement data, which model would you recommend for: \textbf{(i)} an early warning system where explainability to instructors matters, and \textbf{(ii)} a system where prediction accuracy is the top priority? Justify both choices.

\end{enumerate}
